speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Stand in the light, if you mean to be in a play at two. I am not fitting a coat by guess in a tiring-house corner.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The light is yours. The coat is the afternoon's. It is not the king's, and I am not giving you a name to sew into the neck.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: I do not sew names. I sew hems. This hem is sound. The shoulder wants a stitch where yesterday's shrug lives, and yesterday is not a person I can bill.

speaker: john_heminges
text: If it wants a penny, say the penny now, while the book is open. I have just written one cost. I can write two. I would rather not.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: It does not want a penny. A stitch out of my basket is not a charge on the stock. If I begin charging for stitches I shall die rich and unpopular, and I have chosen neither.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then stitch it, and leave the book alone. Eightpence is the morning's cost, and it is not a coat. I will not have a hem married to a copying.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Hold your arm so. There. The shrug is a habit, not a tear. I am not taking the coat home to preach at it.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Good. The book stays at one line. Paint is at two, with the rest of them. Nobody is painted in this room now, and I would like to keep it a true sentence.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Paint at two. I will be in the coat and I will not be in the king. If the stitch holds through the yard, it has done more than most of my promises.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: It will hold. Turn. The other shoulder is honest, which is a rare review from me and I will not repeat it at dinner.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not ask you to. Thank you, Edith. The stock owes you nothing for this, and I owe you the arm held still, which I am bad at.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: You are bad at it, and the stitch is in anyway. Go and let the paper dry. I have a boy's gown to look at that has grown again, and that one may yet cost somebody.
